audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows read Jax or Skill where the page's own whys hand them to you: whys[1] ends 'Mordekaiser's window' but the row said Jax, whys[2] ends 'call it Skill' but the row said Jax, whys[3] ends "Mordekaiser's stage" but the row said Skill, and whys[4] ends "Jax's spike" while the row said Skill.
audit.why: The whys on this page literally name the side at the end of each line and four of them were ignored. The packet chart — Skill / Mordekaiser / Skill / Mordekaiser / Jax / Jax / Jax — agrees with the whys, and the mirror has already flipped to it.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 4 set to Mordekaiser / Skill / Mordekaiser / Jax as one atomic group across both layers, ratings 7/10, 5/10 (unchanged), 7/10, 3/10. phases[2].why and phases[4].why rewritten so the reason matches the new side.

audit.why: Spikes are accurate: your Q+W window at 2-3, Realm of Death at 6, then Jax taking it back at first item and again at two. The page is honest that this is a losing scaling matchup, which matches 48.06% over 1345 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike, the ability the entire page is built around, had no cooldown anywhere. Empower is never mentioned at all. The content layer calls his ultimate 'Grandmaster's Might' in whys[5] and spikes[3].
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 — 17 seconds at rank 1 is a long, punishable window and quantifying it is what makes 'bait it' actionable. Empower is a 3-7s auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast. And Riot's Data Dragon name for his R is Grandmaster-at-Arms; the kit file is the authority on names, and Riot's text for it says every third consecutive attack deals additional magic damage plus an activation that raises armour and magic resist — not that it 'doubles his on-hit'.
audit.corrected: 17s and the dodge-attacks-not-Obliterate rule written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and phases[2].why; Empower's 7s auto reset into breakdown.cooldowns; whys[5] renamed to Grandmaster-at-Arms with Riot's actual wording; dontsFull[1].d states what the ultimate stacks.
sources: enemyKit Jax E cd 17/15/13/11/9 and text
enemyKit Jax W cd and autoReset flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 row promised 'the 1v1 Jax cannot decline' on a row the packet gives to Jax, with no cooldown on your own ultimate.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140s at rank 1. Against a champion whose first item takes the lane back, the honest framing is that you get roughly one attempt and must bank a kill with it, not that the duel is free.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten with the 140s figure and the reason to spend it immediately.

edits.before: Full kit plus Darkness Rise — three hits sets your aura burning and the lane flips. E-drag Jax off his wave and run the Q-auto-E pattern on every Counter Strike cooldown.
edits.after: Darkness Rise is up, but Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and one raised E flips any trade — lead with Obliterate, which it does not dodge, and auto only after it expires.

edits.before: Realm of Death online — the 1v1 Jax cannot decline. R steals 10% of his stats; take the duel whenever Counter Strike is down and the wave is shoved.
edits.after: Realm of Death is your one clean kill and it is 140s at rank 1 — spend it here, because his first item arrives before your second and takes the lane back.

edits.before: At his second item Grandmaster's Might stacks armor and magic resist and doubles his on-hit, out-scaling your flat damage — Jax pulls ahead.
edits.after: At his second item Grandmaster-at-Arms stacks armour and magic resist while every third attack adds magic damage, out-scaling you — Jax pulls ahead.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Counter Strike (E): 17s at rank 1 — dodges attacks, not Obliterate. - Empower (W): 7s auto reset.

edits.before: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 — bait it out with Obliterate first.

notes: NAME DISAGREEMENT with the mirror, needs one ruling. The mirror agent standardised Jax's R to 'Grandmaster's Might' and treated 'Grandmaster at Arms' as the error. Riot's Data Dragon — the kit file and packet.enemyAbilities, which this run defines as the authority on names — gives Grandmaster-at-Arms. I followed the kit and used Grandmaster-at-Arms in whys[5] and dontsFull[1].d. spikes[3].text still says 'Grandmaster's Might (R)' and I left it rather than half-standardise; whichever name is chosen, both fields should end up the same. This is in questionsForUser. Structural note: the whys array is shifted one row against the phase labels from index 2 onward — whys[2] talks about levels 4-5 on the Level 3 row, whys[3] talks about the level-6 ultimate on the Levels 4-5 row, and so on. The packet chart was evidently built from the same shifted narrative, so the sides and the whys agree with each other even though neither agrees with the labels. I aligned to the packet rather than re-sequencing seven whys, but the shift is real and worth a look. No suspect names flagged and none found; the Mordekaiser kit's 'grounding' flag on Q is unsupported by Riot's text, so I made no claim about Obliterate stopping Leap Strike.
